title: Head remodeling passes from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to normal shape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Head remodeling passes from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to normal shape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In canonical variate shape space, the D. japonica head morphology lies between those of G. dorotocephala and S. mediterranea, and octanol-induced S. mediterranea-like G. dorotocephala heads remodel by moving from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to G. dorotocephala morphology.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: DJ morphology lies between GD and SM morphologies in this space, and we observe remodeling that moves from SM morphology to DJ morphology to GD morphology.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent”. Scope: Remodeling octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates, days 10–30

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed trajectory is quantitatively testable, but existing public materials appear to contain summaries and examples rather than the full time-series coordinates. The reported shape space also risks some circularity.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Project longitudinal landmarks from individual pseudo-S. mediterranea worms into a canonical-variate space built independently from wild-type references, then test whether trajectories approach D. japonica before G. dorotocephala. Direct movement or alternative paths would confirm or refute the claimed sequence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Canonical axes can depend on the same group definitions used to describe the path.

The full longitudinal landmark matrix is not clearly public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data existence: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The between-species order and the remodeling path are geometric claims about one shape space. The plot is published, and the scores and landmarks needed to rebuild the axes are not. Small group sizes make that ordering hard to audit from the figure alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute the canonical variate space from the landmarks and test whether Dugesia lies between Girardia and Schmidtea and whether individual trajectories move in that order. A different between-species order, or trajectories that skip or reverse that path, would refute the reported route.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Canonical variate scores depend on the predefined groups and are not in a public table.

With a few animals per class, axis order is sensitive to landmark choice.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.38
operationalizability: 0.74
data existence: 0.34
